edits.content:
# G01 — Error recovery and safe next actions

## Contract

Every `AppErrorCode` has exactly one stable entry in `APP_ERROR_RECOVERY`.
The entry declares:

- `retryable`: whether the host can safely repeat the operation;
- `scope`: `self`, `user`, or `none`;
- `action`: an optional bounded next action.

An `AppError` always exposes `retryable` and `nextAction`. The recovery action
uses only the fixed verbs `retry`, `reauthenticate`, `reconfigure`,
`open-settings`, and `contact-support`. Its only optional parameter is the
bounded `target`; no command, script, shell, exec, argv, or other executable
payload is permitted.

Only transient/self-recoverable classes are retryable. Their action is exactly
`{ kind: 'retry' }`. All other classes require user action and must not request a
retry. `UNKNOWN` deliberately has no action: the original error must be shown
to the user rather than inventing a recovery path.

## Recovery table

| Code | Retryable | Scope | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AUTH_INVALID | no | user | reauthenticate(authentication) |
| AUTH_PERMANENT | no | user | reauthenticate(authentication) |
| TIMEOUT | yes | self | retry |
| RATE_LIMIT | yes | self | retry |
| PERMISSION | no | user | contact-support |
| CHANNEL_UNAVAILABLE | yes | self | retry |
| CONVERSATION_STATE | no | user | reconfigure(provider) |
| NETWORK | yes | self | retry |
| CONFIG | no | user | reconfigure(provider) |
| GATEWAY | yes | self | retry |
| BILLING | no | user | open-settings(billing) |
| OVERLOADED | yes | self | retry |
| MODEL_NOT_FOUND | no | user | reconfigure(model) |
| UNKNOWN | no | user | none; expose original error |

The table is rendered through the existing `HostResponse`/`AppError` error
envelope. It does not introduce another envelope or error type.

# G01 closure: error recovery and next action

## Implementation

`src/lib/error-model.ts` now defines a single, exhaustive recovery policy keyed
by `AppErrorCode`. `APP_ERROR_RECOVERY` is the authoritative table and is
also used to populate every `AppError` instance's `retryable` and
`nextAction` fields.

The policy distinguishes automatic retries from situations that require an
explicit user action. Automatic retries are limited to timeout, rate limit,
channel unavailability, network, gateway, and overload failures. Each of these
has exactly `{ kind: 'retry' }` as its next action.

Authentication failures require reauthentication, configuration and model
selection require a bounded reconfiguration, billing failures open the
billing settings, and permission failures point to support. These instructions
are declarative verbs and bounded targets only; they cannot contain or imply a
shell command, raw script, executable arguments, or arbitrary instruction.

`UNKNOWN` has no next action and is not retryable. The host must expose the
original error to the user. This avoids fabricating a repair when the error
class contains insufficient information.

## Governance

The existing `HostResponse`/`AppError` envelope remains the sole error
representation. The change adds recovery metadata to `AppError` and does not
add a second envelope, error class, or error transport path.

## Verification

The recovery table is checked exhaustively against `APP_ERROR_CODES`. The
validation checks that retryable entries are self-scoped and use exactly the
retry action, non-retryable entries do not use retry, action kinds and targets
are from the fixed allow-list, and `UNKNOWN` has no action. The implementation
also retains the existing type, lint, harness, replay/compare, credential, and
checksum checks.
